title: Detection of chromosome instability by interphase FISH in mouse and human tissues
protocol: Streak a small amount of E. coli onto a selective plate and incubate from 12–16 hours at 37°C to obtain single colonies.
Pick a single colony and inoculate into 10 mL of lysogeny broth (LB) medium containing the selective antibiotic in a 50 mL falcon tube.
Culture poor aeration may contribute to producing a low DNA yield.
Maintain an optimal culture volume to air volume ratio of 1:4 or less.
Grow the culture with vigorous shaking at 37°C in a shaking incubator for 12–16 hours.
Freeze each plasmid by mixing 800 μl of bacteria culture and 200 μl of sterile glycerol.
Harvest bacterial cells by centrifuging at 1792 g (4,000 rpm) for 10 minutes.
Discard the supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the bacterial pellet in 300 μL of GTE buffer and transfer to a 2.2 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 600 μL of freshly made lysis solution and mix gently by inverting.
Incubate on ice for 5 minutes.
Mix gently by inverting the tube four to six times.
Slowly add 500 μL of neutralization buffer drop by drop.
Mix by inverting the tube four to six times (do not vortex).
Incubate on ice for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge at 11200 g (10,000 rpm) for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant using a P1000 pipette to a new 2.2 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 11200 g (10,000 rpm) for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant using a P1000 pipette to a new 1.5 mL centrifuge tube containing 700 μL of ice-cold isopropanol, avoiding any white precipitate material.
Mix by inverting the tube a few times.
Centrifuge at 21952 g (14,000 rpm) for 20 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and wash the DNA pellet with 0.5 mL of 70% ethanol.
Mix by inverting the tube several times.
Centrifuge at 21,952 g (14,000 rpm) for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove as much supernatant as possible with a pipette and air-dry the pellet at 20°C–25°C for 10 min.
Once the pellet turns from white to translucent in appearance, dissolve the DNA into 100 μL of nuclease-free water by gentle occasional tapping of the tube.
Add 1 μL of RNAse (100 ug/mL) and incubate for 30 min at 37°C.
Precipitate the DNA in a mix of 1/10 vol 3 M sodium acetate and 2.5 vol of 100% ethanol for 60 min at −80°C.
Centrifuge at 21,952 g (14,000 rpm) for 15 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and wash the DNA pellet with 0.5 mL of 70% ethanol.
Centrifuge at 21,952 g (14,000 rpm) for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and dissolve the DNA into 100 μL of nuclease-free water.
Set up the Nick translation reaction in a final volume of 50 μL on ice.
Vortex and centrifuge the tube for 10 seconds.
Incubate the tube for 90 minutes at 16°C.
Place the reaction on ice after incubation.
Run 5 μl of the mix in a 1% agarose gel to determine product size distribution.
Incubate the mix for another 30 min at 16°C if the size of the bulk of the fragments is larger than 500 bp.
Inactivate DNaseI by incubating the mix at 75°C for 10 min if the size of the bulk of the fragments is not larger than 500 bp.
Purify the DNA with a PCR purification kit and elute in 60 μL of nuclease-free water.
Precipitate the DNA in a mix of 1/10 vol 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2), 2.5 vol of 100% ethanol, and 1 μg of Cot-1 DNA.
Incubate from 12-16 h at -20°C for precipitation.
Centrifuge the mixture at 21,952 g (14,000 rpm) for 15 min at 4°C.
Wash the pellet with 500 μL of 70% ethanol and allow to air dry.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 μL of nuclease-free water.
Store the DNA at -20°C.
Cut FFPE tissue sections of 4–6 μm and mount them on poly-L-lysine-coated or positively-charged glass slides.
Pretreat FFPE tissue sections for 3 hours.
Incubate the pretreated slides for 8–16 hours.
Melt the paraffin by incubating the slides at 65°C for 12-16 hours.
Deparaffinize the tissue slides in a xylene bath and incubate for 3 minutes at 65°C.
Change the xylene bath and repeat once.
Tap gently on a paper towel to draw off excess liquid.
Place the slides in 100% ethanol for 3 minutes at 20-25°C.
Change the ethanol bath and repeat once.
Tap off excess liquid.
Place the slides in 80% ethanol for 3 minutes at 20-25°C.
Tap off excess liquid.
Place the slides in 70% ethanol for 3 minutes at 20-25°C.
Heat water bath and pre-treatment solution (10 mM citrate buffer, pH 6.0) to 95-99°C in a plastic Coplin jar.
Immerse deparaffinized sections into 0.2 N HCl for 20 minutes at 20-25°C.
Incubate slides in pre-heated pre-treatment solution for 20 minutes at 95-99°C.
Allow the slides to cool in the pre-treatment solution for 15 minutes at 20-25°C.
Wash the slides in a Coplin jar with 1× PBS and soak for 3 minutes at 20-25°C.
Replace 1× PBS and soak sections for another 3 minutes.
Dry the slides by touching gently the bottom edge and wiping the underside with a paper towel.
Cover the pre-treated tissue with 40 μL of ready to use pepsin.
Incubate samples for 30 min at 37°C.
Place the slides in 70% ethanol for 3 min at 20°C–25°C.
Change ethanol bath and repeat once.
Tap off the excess liquid.
Place the slides in 80% ethanol for 3 min at 20°C–25°C.
Tap off the excess liquid.
Place the slides in 96% ethanol for 3 min at 20°C–25°C.
Air-dry the slides from 2 to 5 min.
Place the slide on a 45°C–50°C slide warmer to allow the remaining ethanol to evaporate.
Thaw labeled probe and Vysis IntelliFISH hybridization buffer (08N87-001) at 20°C–25°C.
Prepare the probe mixture with 1 μL of labeled probe, 3 μL of nuclease-free water, and 7 μL of hybridization buffer.
Vortex the mix and centrifuge using a micro-centrifuge for 2-3 s at maximum speed.
Apply 10 μL of the probe mixture to the center of each tissue section.
Immediately apply a coverslip over the probe mixture.
Apply 10 μL of probe mixture to the slide with mounted tissue.
Place an appropriately sized coverslip over the probe mixture immediately.
Remove any bubbles present under the coverslip gently.
Seal the edges of the coverslip with rubber cement, ensuring it straddles the edge.
Begin the denaturation-hybridization program using the ThermoBrite instrument.
Incubate the slides for 12–16 hours to allow hybridization.
Carefully remove the rubber cement seal by pulling one corner with forceps.
Pre-warm the wash solution (0.4× SSC/0.3% NP-40) in a Coplin jar at 75°C for at least 30 minutes prior to use.
Prepare a second container of 2× SSC/0.1% NP-40 at 20°C–25°C.
Remove the rubber cement seal with forceps by gently pulling one corner of the seal.
Soak the slides in a Coplin jar with 2× SSC at 20°C–25°C to remove the coverslip.
If necessary, tap the slide gently in the Coplin jar to loosen the stuck coverslip.
Slide the blade of a scalpel under one corner of the slide and lift it gently before immersing into the Coplin jar if the coverslip remains stuck.
Immediately place each slide into the 0.4× SSC/0.3% NP-40 wash solution at 73 ± 1°C after removing the coverslip.
Agitate the slide for 5 seconds in the wash solution.
Do not wash more than four slides in each Coplin jar.
Wash the slide in 0.4× SSC/0.3% NP-40 wash solution at 73 ± 1°C for 2 minutes.
Place the slide in 2× SSC/0.1% NP-40 wash solution at 20°C–25°C.
Agitate the slide for 5 seconds and let it stand for 5 minutes.
Air dry the slide in the dark.
Apply 10 μL of counterstain dye (0.5 vol 4′,6-diamidino-2-phenylindole DAPI II/0.5 vol antifade) to each slide.
Mount the slides with a 25×50 mm coverslip.
Analyze FISH signals at 1000× magnification using appropriate filters.
Select a representative area of tissue with good nuclear distribution for analysis.
Select representative areas of tissue with good nuclear distribution for FISH analysis.
Highlight single nuclei that meet criteria using white dashed lines; scale bars, 10 μm.
Capture images using a Leica DM5500B fluorescence microscope with a 100× objective and Cytovision v7.4 software.
Enumerate the number of signals within each nucleus using a 100× objective and prescribed filters.
Focus up and down to find all signals present in the nucleus.
Move to another representative area for enumeration until 200–300 tumor cells have been analyzed.
Perform FISH imaging on a Leica DM5500B equipped with a 100× oil-immersion objective, DAPI, Aqua, Green and Orange fluorescence filter cubes.
Connect the microscope to a PC running Zytovision image analysis system with focus motor and Z stack software.
Visualize FISH signals of each nucleus under the microscope using its specific filter.
Count and annotate every FISH signal for each nucleus.
Compute a summary index based on all examined cells.
Select representative images from several tissue areas to account for at least 200–300 nuclei signals.
Choose only intact nuclei that are not folded, overlapped or obstructed by debris.
Evaluate the total number of signals for each nucleus using the probes designed.
Annotate the total number of signals to reach a final count of 200–300 nuclei.
Calculate the CS value for each chromosome probe [e.g., CS1, CS2, or CS3] using the formula: CSChrp = 1 / n ∑ [( eChrp − oChrp )].
Sum individual CS values to obtain the CSC for a given sample: CSC = (CSChrp + CSChrq + CSChrr).
Alternatively, calculate an overall mean CSc for each sample by dividing the sum of all CSC values by the total number of nuclei evaluated.
